alternatives.argument: Define the periodic finite-grid stencil with wraparound and define the two-dimensional Dirichlet stencil by the supplied rectangular grid convention. Apply the θ update δ_tU+A_h((1−θ)U^n+θU^{n+1})=(1−θ)F^n+θF^{n+1}; for Dirichlet data split the full stencil into its zero-boundary matrix plus the known boundary vector c_h(B), giving the stated endpoint rows.

Set τ to the exact-sample update minus endpoint-weighted f. Substitute u_t+A u=f at both endpoints. For each coordinate, symmetric Taylor expansion gives |δ_h²u−u_xx|≤h²||u_xxxx||∞/12. The time quotient is the average of g=u_t; its difference from the endpoint θ-weight is bounded by k||g′||∞ when θ≠1/2. At θ=1/2, subtract the endpoint linear interpolant; its pointwise error is ≤||g″||∞(t−a)(b−t)/2, whose average is k²||g″||∞/12. Adding these contributions gives both residual bounds, including boundary-adjacent rows because boundary samples are exact.

For each periodic multi-index ℓ substitute φℓ(i)=exp(2πiΣℓ_j i_j/N_j); opposite neighbors multiply by conjugate phases, giving λℓ=4Σκ_jh_j⁻²sin²(πℓ_j/N_j). Substitution into the θ update yields gθ=(1−(1−θ)kλ)/(1+θkλ). Finite geometric sums show distinct modes orthogonal; their count equals the grid dimension, so they form a basis.

Rearrange each Dirichlet row. Under k(1−θ)Σκ_j/h_j²≤1/2, the old center, old neighbors, and future-boundary coefficients are nonnegative. Given nonnegative data, a strictly negative minimum of the implicit solution makes its M-matrix row strictly negative, contradicting the nonnegative right-hand side. Induct on time for positivity, then compare with the constant solutions equal to the global initial/boundary maximum and minimum. In the homogeneous-boundary subcase at θ=1/2 the sufficient positivity restriction is finite, while the separate weighted-L2 energy theorem applies for every positive step.

Take the weighted inner product of δU+kA Uθ=kq with Uθ and use <δU,Uθ>=1/2(||U¹||²−||U⁰||²)+(θ−1/2)||δU||². Positive semidefinite A and θ≥1/2 give 1/2(b²−a²)≤k||q|| max(a,b). If b≤a contraction is immediate; if b>a divide by (a+b)/2 to get b−a≤2k||q||. Set q=0 and iterate.

Subtract the numerical update from the exact sampled update; exact initial and boundary data give e⁰=0 and zero boundary error, while the source in the error equation is τ. Apply the forced energy estimate at each step and sum to get ||e^m||≤2kΣ||τ^n||. Since the weighted interior grid mass is hxhy(Nx−1)(Ny−1)<LxLy, ||τ^n||_h≤√(LxLy)||τ^n||∞. Sum over mk≤T and insert the local residual bound.

alternatives.argument: The local finite Fourier lemma gives λℓ=4Σκ_jh_j⁻²sin²(πℓ_j/N_j)≤4Σκ_j/h_j². With ΔtΣκ_j/h_j²≤1/2, each forward-Euler factor 1−Δtλℓ lies in [−1,1], so the orthogonal Fourier basis yields L2 nonexpansion. If all N_j are even, the joint Nyquist mode attains the eigenvalue bound and has factor 1−4ΔtΣκ_j/h_j², which is below −1 above the threshold.

At the even-grid Nyquist eigenvalue λ=4κ/h², the θ=1/2 multiplier is (1−2κΔt/h²)/(1+2κΔt/h²). Its magnitude is at most one because |1−z/2|≤1+z/2 for z≥0; with fixed Δt>0 and h→0 the ratio tends to −1, so high-mode damping tends to zero.

For each two-dimensional Dirichlet row, rewrite the θ equation with coefficient 1−2(1−θ)Δt(κx/hx²+κy/hy²) on the old center. Under the stated positivity condition all explicit coefficients are nonnegative. The implicit matrix preserves nonnegativity by the negative-minimum contradiction. Inductively the solution stays nonnegative; comparison with constant upper and lower grid solutions bounds it by the extrema of initial and boundary data. In the homogeneous-boundary subcase at θ=1/2 the sufficient positivity restriction is finite, while the separate weighted-L2 energy theorem applies for every positive step.
